claims.proposition: External net WHEAT demand can make a buy-before-rival and unwind-after-rival pressure position profitable while increasing the rival's acquisition cost.
claims.scope: Independent pinned WHEAT pricing model and constructed demand controls; this is a stress mechanism, not a current TITAN production-policy or field-EV claim.
claims.disposition: Keep the mechanism as a gauntlet/stress hypothesis and measure both seats against current V4; do not promote the included pressure agent as canonical policy from constructed receipts alone.

claims.proposition: Player buying can make WHEAT literally unavailable by driving market inventory to zero.
claims.scope: Pinned official WHEAT BUY_PRODUCT availability semantics only; scarcity pricing can still raise acquisition cost.
claims.disposition: Do not build a WHEAT-unavailability/starvation strategy; reason in price pressure rather than stockout.
claims.next_gate: Re-open only if a new engine introduces a market-stock availability check.

anchors: There is no market-stock availability check on WHEAT buys. Inventory can cross zero.
“Starvation” therefore cannot make WHEAT unavailable; it can only raise the rival's acquisition cost.

claims.proposition: A player can profit from a pure self-created WHEAT scarcity position by buying and later selling the same quantity with no intervening market flow.
claims.scope: Pinned official per-unit WHEAT quote semantics with no intervening external market flow; external demand is explicitly outside this falsification.
claims.disposition: Do not treat self-only WHEAT buy/unwind as an intrinsic money printer; any edge must come from intervening external net flow or another mechanism.
claims.next_gate: Re-open only with authenticated engine changes or a witness containing explicit intervening market flow.

anchors: A self-created WHEAT squeeze is exactly reversible:
